Q1: Calcium peroxide exhibits known hazards (Tier 1) for oral, dermal, and eye exposure according to the GHS. Additionally, an expanded perspective (Tier 2) indicates potential inhalation hazards. However, significant data deficiencies (Tier 4) exist for carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, reproductive hazards, environmental hazards, endocrine disruption, and organ/systemic hazards.
Q2: Calcium peroxide is not currently listed on major "Lists of Concern." This absence may, in part, reflect the notable data deficiencies across several hazard classes, suggesting the chemical may be under-studied in certain areas.
Q3: Calcium peroxide appears generally well-characterized, evidenced by a precise molecular formula (CaO2), classification as a 'Small Molecule,' and a substantial number of scientific literature references (4389), which is considerably above average. However, despite this general characterization, its hazard profile is incomplete due to data deficiencies (Tier 4) in four out of seven hazard categories.
